description: The humidity–DL MCS association should remain screened out because it was not robust to temporal-cycle control.
mechanistic_interpretations: Humidity may co-vary with a recurring environmental cycle that also affects the RF state, without being the direct explanatory variable.
alternative_explanations: A shared time-of-day structure may create the inverse association.
A slow temporal trend may make humidity and DL MCS appear related even when their short-term variations are not linked.
The discrete RF outcome may respond to other time-varying conditions that happen to co-occur with humidity changes.
falsification_tests: same_clock_matched_control: compare candidate events with controls matched to the same clock-time structure.
trend_diurnal_adjustment: test the residual association after a prespecified temporal-trend and diurnal adjustment.
blocked_temporal_replication: require the adjusted direction to remain stable across contiguous temporal blocks.
uncertainties: The present evidence cannot separate a humidity-specific relationship from shared temporal structure.
